usage.verb_pattern: The standard pattern is compliment someone on something: She complimented me on my presentation.
usage.noun_pattern: A compliment is normally countable: give someone a compliment.
usage.compliments_plural: Compliments can mean greetings, praise, or good wishes in expressions such as compliments to the chef.
usage.spelling: Compliment with i means praise; complement with e means complete, enhance, or form a matching counterpart.
usage.adjective: Complimentary can mean expressing praise or provided free of charge.
usage.register: Natural in both everyday and professional communication.

ja: 人の外見・能力・行為・所有物などを褒める言葉
人への敬意・評価・称賛を表す行為
人の外見・能力・成果などについて好意的な評価を伝える
compliments の形で、挨拶・賛辞・よろしくとの言葉
with someone’s compliments の形で、厚意により無料で贈られたこと
en: a favorable remark about someone’s appearance, ability, conduct, achievement, or possessions
an act expressing admiration, respect, or approval
to express a favorable judgment about someone or something associated with them
in the plural, greetings, praise, or good wishes sent to someone
in with someone’s compliments, provided as a gift or without charge

nuance.ja: compliment は、特定の長所・外見・成果について伝える個別の褒め言葉であり、通常は好意的・誠実なものとして理解される。flattery は過剰・不誠実で、利益を得る目的を持つ可能性を示唆する点で異なる。Your English is excellent. は compliment になり得るが、相手から何かを得るために大げさに言えば flattery になり得る。動詞では compliment someone on something とし、compliment on someone とはしない。I’ll take that as a compliment. は、曖昧または少し批判的な発言を、あえて褒め言葉として受け取る表現である。
nuance.en: A compliment is an individual favorable remark about a particular quality, appearance, possession, or achievement and is normally understood as friendly and sincere. Flattery differs in suggesting possible exaggeration, insincerity, or self-interested motivation. Your English is excellent can be a compliment, but it may become flattery if deliberately exaggerated to obtain an advantage. The verb pattern is compliment someone on something, not compliment on someone. I’ll take that as a compliment humorously or confidently treats an ambiguous or mildly critical remark as praise.

ja: compliment：外見・能力・成果などについて人に伝える、個別の褒め言葉。
praise：価値ある行為・性質・成果を称賛すること。compliment より広く強い場合がある。
flattery：相手を喜ばせたり利益を得たりするための、過剰・不誠実になり得る称賛。
commend：人の行為・成果を正式に高く評価する。
congratulate：成功・合格・結婚などの喜ばしい出来事について祝意を伝える。
admire：人・物の性質や成果を優れていると感じ、尊敬・感嘆する。
complimentary：称賛を表す、または無料で提供される。
complement：別の物を補い、全体を完成・向上させる。compliment とは別語。
en: a compliment is an individual favorable remark about appearance, ability, or achievement.
praise is approval of valuable conduct, qualities, or achievements and can be broader or stronger.
flattery is potentially excessive or insincere praise intended to please or influence someone.
commend means formally expressing approval of someone’s conduct or achievement.
congratulate means expressing pleasure at someone’s success or happy event.
admire means regarding someone or something with respect, approval, or wonder.
complimentary means expressing praise or provided free of charge.
complement means completing or enhancing something and is distinct from compliment.

etymology.ja: フランス語 compliment、イタリア語 complimento を経て英語に入り、さらにラテン語 complere「満たす、完成させる」に関係する。もとは礼儀上の義務を「満たす」挨拶・敬意の表明を指し、そこから人を喜ばせる好意的な言葉という意味が発達した。complement も同じラテン語系統に属するが、complement は「欠けた部分を満たして完成させるもの」、compliment は「褒め言葉」と意味・綴りが分かれた。
etymology.en: Compliment entered English through French compliment and Italian complimento and is ultimately related to Latin complere, to fill or complete. It originally referred to a ceremonial expression that fulfilled a social obligation of politeness or respect. From this developed the modern sense of a favorable remark that pleases another person. Complement belongs to the same Latin word family but developed the meaning something that completes or enhances, while compliment became the word for praise.

note.ja: 人の行動・性質・成果を価値あるものとして評価し、称賛すること。
note.en: Approval expressed for a person’s conduct, qualities, or achievements.

note.ja: 優れた行為・業績に対する、比較的正式な称賛・表彰。
note.en: Relatively formal praise or recognition for admirable conduct or achievement.

note.ja: 人物・功績への尊敬・感謝を、公に表明する言葉や行為。
note.en: A public statement or act expressing admiration or gratitude for a person or achievement.

note.ja: 人を喜ばせる好意的な発言。文脈によってはお世辞の含みを持つ。
note.en: A favorable statement that pleases someone and may, depending on context, suggest flattery.

note.ja: 功績に対して与えられる公的な称賛・賞・栄誉。
note.en: Public praise, an award, or an honor granted in recognition of achievement.

ja: She complimented me on my presentation. — 彼女は私のプレゼンテーションを褒めてくれた。
He received several compliments on his new jacket. — 彼は新しいジャケットについて、いくつもの褒め言葉をもらった。
I wasn’t sure whether her remark was a compliment or a criticism. — 彼女の発言が褒め言葉なのか批判なのか、私には分からなかった。

He received several compliments on his new jacket.
I wasn’t sure whether her remark was a compliment or a criticism.
The client complimented the legal team on its clear and practical advice.

grammar.countability: countable for a young deer; uncountable for the color

usage.animal: As a countable noun, fawn normally means a young deer, especially during its first year.
usage.color: Fawn can name a light yellowish-brown color and can modify another noun.
usage.preposition: In the flattering sense, fawn is normally followed by over, on, or upon.
usage.evaluation: The verb is strongly disapproving and suggests excessive, servile, or self-interested admiration.
usage.transitivity: Do not normally say fawn someone; use fawn over or fawn on someone.

ja: 生後おおむね一年以内の鹿の子、子鹿
薄い黄褐色・淡い茶色
歓心・利益・承認を得るため、人にへつらう
人を過度に褒めたり、ちやほやしたりする
相手に従属的な態度で愛想や称賛を示す
en: a young deer, especially one in its first year
a light yellowish-brown color
to behave flatteringly toward someone in order to gain favor, approval, or advantage
to give someone excessive praise or admiring attention
to display affection or admiration in a servile manner

nuance.ja: 動詞 fawn は、単に人を admire「尊敬する」または praise「称賛する」のではなく、相手の権力・地位・人気などから利益を得ようとして、過度にへりくだった称賛を示すことを表す。fawn over は、相手を大げさに褒めてちやほやする行動に焦点を置き、fawn on/upon もほぼ同じ意味だが、やや文語的に響く場合がある。fawning は a fawning admirer や a fawning tone のように、卑屈な追従を表す強い批判語である。子鹿を表す名詞の fawn には、この否定的評価はない。
nuance.en: As a verb, fawn does not merely mean admire or praise. It suggests exaggerated and servile approval directed toward someone whose power, status, or popularity may provide an advantage. Fawn over emphasizes lavish attention and praise. Fawn on or upon has nearly the same meaning and may sound somewhat more literary. Fawning is strongly critical in expressions such as a fawning admirer or a fawning tone. The noun referring to a young deer carries none of this negative evaluation.

ja: fawn：名詞では子鹿。動詞では、利益や歓心を得るため人に過度にへつらう。
flatter：人を喜ばせたり利益を得たりするため、実際以上に褒める。
adore：人・物を深く愛し、非常に好む。へつらいとは限らない。
gush over：人・物について、興奮して大げさに褒める。
grovel：許し・利益などを得るため、卑屈に振る舞う。
kowtow：権力者に対して過度に服従・追従する。
suck up to：利益を得るため目上の人にへつらう、非常に口語的な表現。
sycophancy：権力者の歓心を買うための卑屈で不誠実な追従。
en: fawn means a young deer or, as a verb, giving someone excessive and servile admiration to gain favor.
flatter means praising someone excessively to please them or obtain an advantage.
adore means loving or liking someone or something deeply and does not necessarily imply servility.
gush over means praising someone or something with excited and excessive enthusiasm.
grovel means behaving with extreme humility or submission to obtain forgiveness or advantage.
kowtow means showing excessive obedience or submission to someone powerful.
suck up to is a highly informal expression for flattering a superior to gain an advantage.
sycophancy is servile and insincere praise intended to gain favor with someone powerful.

etymology.ja: 名詞 fawn「子鹿」は古フランス語 faon を経て、ラテン語 fetus「子を産むこと、子、胎児」に関係する語から英語に入った。一方、動詞 fawn「へつらう」は別系統で、古英語 fagnian「喜ぶ、うれしそうに振る舞う」に由来し、fain「喜んで」と同族である。喜びを示して相手にまとわりつく行動から、権力者などに愛想よくへつらう意味へ発達した。したがって、子鹿が従順に見えるため「へつらう」の意味が生まれたという説明は、直接の語源ではない。
etymology.en: The noun fawn, a young deer, came through Old French faon and is ultimately related to a Latin word connected with fetus, offspring, or giving birth. The verb fawn, meaning behave servilely, has a separate history. It derives from Old English fagnian, to rejoice or show delight, and is related to fain. From displaying eager pleasure and affection, the verb developed the sense of behaving ingratiatingly toward a powerful person. The flattering sense therefore did not directly originate from the submissive appearance of a young deer.

note.ja: 相手を喜ばせたり動かしたりする目的で、過剰な称賛を与える。
note.en: To give someone excessive praise in order to please or influence them.

note.ja: 人・作品などについて、感情をあふれさせて大げさに褒める。
note.en: To praise a person or work with overflowing and often excessive enthusiasm.

note.ja: 利益・許しを得るため、自尊心を捨てたように卑屈に振る舞う。
note.en: To behave with humiliating submission in order to obtain advantage or forgiveness.

note.ja: 権力・権威を持つ人に過度の服従や追従を示す。
note.en: To display excessive obedience or deference toward a powerful authority.

note.ja: 目上の人から利益を得るためにへつらう、くだけた批判表現。
note.en: A strongly informal and critical expression for flattering a superior to gain favor.

ja: We saw a doe and her fawn at the edge of the forest. — 森の縁で、雌鹿とその子鹿を見かけた。
The guests fawned over the famous actor throughout the evening. — 客たちはその晩ずっと、有名俳優を大げさにちやほやしていた。
He refuses to fawn on senior managers merely to advance his career. — 彼は出世のためだけに上級管理職へへつらうことを拒んでいる。
The journalist criticized the interview for its fawning tone. — その記者は、インタビューの追従的な口調を批判した。
A patent applicant must rely on evidence and legal argument, not fawn over the examiner in the hope of securing allowance. — 特許出願人は、特許査定を期待して審査官にへつらうのではなく、証拠と法的主張に依拠しなければならない。

The guests fawned over the famous actor throughout the evening.

patterns: suck up to the boss / teacher
suck up to someone for + benefit
suck up to someone by + gerund
try to suck up to someone
accuse someone of sucking up to + person
have no need to suck up to anyone

usage.object_position: The person being flattered follows to: suck up to the manager.
usage.inseparability: The expression is not separated; do not say suck the manager up to.
usage.evaluation: It is strongly disapproving and imputes a selfish motive to the person’s politeness or praise.
usage.noun: The noun suck-up is hyphenated and refers disparagingly to a person who behaves this way.
usage.separate_literal_use: Suck up without to can literally mean draw in liquid, dust, or air and must be distinguished from this idiom.
usage.register: Highly informal and potentially insulting; ingratiate oneself with is appropriate in formal contexts.

ja: 利益を得るため、目上の人・権力者にお世辞を言う
昇進・評価・許可などを期待して、人の機嫌を取る
過度な称賛や従順な態度によって歓心を買おうとする
人に取り入るため、不誠実な親切・同意・追従を示す
en: to flatter a superior or powerful person in order to obtain an advantage
to seek promotion, approval, or permission by pleasing someone
to gain favor through excessive praise or submissive behavior
to display insincere kindness, agreement, or devotion in order to ingratiate oneself

nuance.ja: suck up to は、相手への称賛が不誠実で、利益を得るための行動だと決めつける強い批判表現である。単に上司へ礼儀正しく接したり、正当に評価したりするだけでは suck up to とはいわない。He’s sucking up to the boss. は「あいつは上司にごまをすっている」と、その人の動機や人格まで否定的に評価する。そのため本人へ直接 Stop sucking up. と言えば侮辱的になり得る。主にアメリカ英語でよく使われるが、広く理解される。正式な文脈では seek favor with、ingratiate oneself with、use flattery to influence などが適切である。
nuance.en: Suck up to strongly criticizes praise or politeness as insincere conduct motivated by personal advantage. Merely treating a manager courteously or offering deserved praise does not amount to sucking up. He’s sucking up to the boss negatively judges both the conduct and the person’s motive or character. Directly telling someone Stop sucking up can therefore be insulting. The expression is especially common in American English but is widely understood. In formal contexts, seek favor with, ingratiate oneself with, or use flattery to influence is more appropriate.

ja: suck up to：利益を得るため目上の人にへつらう。非常に口語的で批判的。
flatter：人を喜ばせたり動かしたりするため、実際以上に褒める。
fawn over：人に過度な称賛・注目を示し、ちやほやする。
ingratiate oneself with：歓心を買うため、意図的に人へ好印象を与える。より形式的。
curry favor with：利益を得るため、権力者などの機嫌を取る。
brown-nose：目上の人に卑屈にへつらう。suck up to より下品に響き得る。
butter up：頼み事を通すため、お世辞で相手の機嫌を取る。
be courteous to：人に礼儀正しく接する。自己利益や不誠実さは含まない。
en: suck up to means flattering a superior for personal advantage and is highly informal and critical.
flatter means praising someone excessively in order to please or influence them.
fawn over means giving someone excessive and servile admiration or attention.
ingratiate oneself with formally means deliberately making oneself agreeable to gain another person’s favor.
curry favor with means trying to gain advantage by pleasing someone powerful.
brown-nose means flattering a superior servilely and may sound cruder than suck up to.
butter up means using flattery to prepare someone to grant a request.
be courteous to means treating someone politely without implying selfish motivation or insincerity.

etymology.ja: suck は古英語 sūcan「吸う」に由来する。液体などを自分の方へ吸い寄せる物理的意味から、suck up には「吸い上げる」という意味が生まれた。一方、人にへつらう suck up の正確な比喩的成立過程は明確ではない。20世紀のアメリカ口語として広まり、権力者へ過度に接近して好意を得ようとする行動を表すようになった。名詞 suck-up は、この句動詞から作られた比較的新しい人物呼称である。
etymology.en: Suck comes from Old English sucan, meaning to draw in by suction. The physical meaning produced the literal phrasal verb suck up, as when a machine sucks up liquid or dust. The precise figurative development of suck up for servile flattery is not entirely clear. It became established in twentieth-century American informal usage for behavior intended to gain the favor of someone powerful. The disparaging noun suck-up was subsequently formed from the phrasal verb.

note.ja: 利益・受容を得るため、人に好かれるよう意図的に振る舞う形式的な表現。
note.en: A formal expression for deliberately making oneself agreeable to another person in order to gain acceptance or advantage.

note.ja: 権力者などを喜ばせる行動によって、好意・利益を得ようとする。
note.en: To seek favor or advantage by acting in ways intended to please someone influential.

note.ja: 昇進・利益などを求め、上司や権力者に卑屈にへつらう。
note.en: To flatter a superior servilely in pursuit of promotion or another advantage.

note.ja: 相手に過度な称賛・愛想・注目を示し、歓心を買おうとする。
note.en: To give someone excessive praise, affection, or attention in an attempt to gain favor.

note.ja: 要求・頼み事を受け入れさせるため、あらかじめ人にお世辞を言う。
note.en: To flatter someone in preparation for asking them to grant a request.

grammar.transitivity: modal auxiliary followed by a bare infinitive
patterns: you / he / she / they shall + bare infinitive

usage.bare_infinitive: Shall is followed by the base form without to: shall go, not shall to go.
usage.third_person: It does not take -s: she shall, not she shalls.
usage.questions: In questions, shall precedes the subject without do: Shall we begin?
usage.negative: Shall not is standard; shan’t is chiefly British and relatively uncommon in formal writing.
usage.defective_modal: Shall has no infinitive, participle, or gerund forms.
usage.should: Should developed historically as the past form of shall, but in modern English it has largely independent meanings.

ja: Shall I ...? の形で、自分が何かをすることを申し出る
Shall we ...? の形で、相手と一緒に行うことを提案する
特に形式的・伝統的なイギリス英語で、I / we の未来を表す
強い決意・約束・命令を表す
契約・法令などで、当事者に義務を課す
規則・宣言などで、将来必ず生じる結果を厳粛に述べる
en: in Shall I ...?, to offer to perform an action
in Shall we ...?, to suggest a joint action
especially in formal or traditional British English, to express the future with I or we
to express strong determination, a promise, or a command
in contracts or legislation, to impose an obligation on a party
in rules or declarations, to state a future consequence solemnly or authoritatively

nuance.ja: 現代の日常英語では、単純未来を表す shall は大幅に減少し、通常は I’ll、we’ll が使われる。一方、Shall I open the window? は申し出、Shall we begin? は提案として現在も重要で、特にイギリス英語で自然である。アメリカ英語では Shall we ...? は理解されるが、Should we ...?、Would you like me to ...?、Do you want to ...? などが選ばれることも多い。契約書の shall は義務を示す伝統的用法だが、未来・義務・権利・宣言のいずれかが不明確になることがある。したがって、義務なら must、将来の事実なら will、裁量・許可なら may と書き分ける方針も広がっている。
nuance.en: In present-day everyday English, shall has largely disappeared as a neutral future marker and I’ll or we’ll is normally used instead. Shall I open the window? remains important as an offer, and Shall we begin? as a suggestion, especially in British English. American speakers understand these constructions but may prefer Should we ...?, Would you like me to ...?, or Do you want to ...?. Contractual shall traditionally imposes an obligation, but it can become ambiguous among obligation, futurity, entitlement, and declaration. Many plain-language approaches therefore distinguish must for obligation, will for future fact, and may for permission or discretion.

ja: shall：申し出・提案を表し、形式的文体では未来・決意・法的義務にも使われる。
will：現代英語で未来・意思・予測を表す一般的な助動詞。
should：助言・望ましさ・蓋然性・弱い義務を表す。現代では shall と別個の助動詞。
must：強い義務・必要性を明確に表す。法的義務の shall の代替にもなる。
may：許可・裁量・可能性を表す。義務は表さない。
can：能力・可能性・日常的な許可を表す。
Shall I ...?：自分が何かをすることを相手に申し出る。
Shall we ...?：相手と一緒に行う行動を提案する。
en: shall expresses offers and suggestions and can mark futurity, determination, or legal obligation in formal styles.
will is the ordinary modern modal for futurity, intention, and prediction.
should expresses advice, desirability, probability, or a weaker obligation and now functions independently from shall.
must clearly expresses strong obligation or necessity and may replace obligatory shall in legal drafting.
may expresses permission, discretion, or possibility rather than obligation.
can expresses ability, possibility, or informal permission.
Shall I ...? offers to perform an action for or with the listener.
Shall we ...? proposes an action to be performed jointly.

etymology.ja: 古英語 sceal「負っている、義務がある、～すべきである」に由来し、原義は未来ではなく義務・必要性だった。ドイツ語 sollen、オランダ語 zullen などと同族である。「義務として行うべきこと」が将来実現するという関係から、未来を表す助動詞としても使われるようになった。過去形 sceolde は現代英語の should になったが、should は助言・蓋然性など独自の意味を発達させ、現在では単純に shall の過去形とはいえない。
etymology.en: Shall comes from Old English sceal, meaning owe, be obliged, or be required. Its original force concerned obligation and necessity rather than simple future time. It is related to German sollen and Dutch zullen. Because something owed or required was expected to be performed later, shall developed into a marker of futurity. The old past form sceolde became should, but should developed independent meanings of advice, expectation, and probability and is no longer simply the past tense of shall.

note.ja: 未来・意思・予測を表す現代英語の標準的な助動詞。
note.en: The standard modern modal for future events, intentions, and predictions.

note.ja: 規則・必要性・命令に基づく強い義務を、shall より明確に表す。
note.en: Expresses strong obligation arising from a rule, necessity, or command more explicitly than shall.

note.ja: 望ましい行動・助言・予想を表し、通常は must より弱い。
note.en: Expresses advisable conduct or expectation and is normally weaker than must.

note.ja: 法律・規則・契約などによって行為を義務付けられていることを明示する。
note.en: Explicitly states that an action is mandatory under a law, rule, or agreement.

note.ja: 正式な予定・指示・取り決めによって、ある行為をすることになっていると表す。
note.en: Indicates an action scheduled or required by a formal plan, instruction, or arrangement.

ja: Shall I help you? — お手伝いしましょうか
Shall I open the window? — 窓を開けましょうか
Shall we begin? — 始めましょうか
Shall we discuss this later? — これは後で話し合いましょうか
I shall return — 私は必ず戻る
we shall see — いずれ分かるだろう
you shall not pass — お前を通しはしない
the buyer shall pay — 買主は支払わなければならない
shall be entitled to — ～する権利を有するものとする
shall be deemed to — ～とみなされるものとする
shall not disclose — 開示してはならない
as the court shall determine — 裁判所が決定するところに従って
en: Shall I help you?
Shall I open the window?
Shall we begin?
Shall we discuss this later?
I shall return
we shall see
you shall not pass
the buyer shall pay
shall be entitled to
shall be deemed to
shall not disclose
as the court shall determine

ja: Shall I carry that bag for you? — そのかばんをお持ちしましょうか。
Shall we meet in the hotel lobby at nine? — 9時にホテルのロビーで会いましょうか。
We shall continue despite the difficulties. — 困難があっても、私たちは必ず続ける。
The licensee shall pay the royalty within thirty days of receiving the invoice. — ライセンシーは、請求書を受領してから30日以内にロイヤルティーを支払わなければならない。

In plain legal drafting, “The applicant must submit the document” may state the obligation more clearly than “The applicant shall submit the document.” — 平易な法律文書では、The applicant shall submit the document よりも The applicant must submit the document の方が義務を明確に示せる場合がある。
en: Shall I carry that bag for you?
Shall we meet in the hotel lobby at nine?
We shall continue despite the difficulties.
The licensee shall pay the royalty within thirty days of receiving the invoice.
In plain legal drafting, “The applicant must submit the document” may state the obligation more clearly than “The applicant shall submit the document.”
